Trevor Connelly is 20, a year removed from the AHL, and already one of the Golden Knights' more useful forwards. He has seven goals and 12 points in 21 games, including the late winner in Detroit that capped what SportsGrid called a road trip to remember, and his toe-drag highlights have become a fixture on the team's channels.

The underlying numbers back up the buzz. Vegas takes 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, eight points better than without him, and his on-ice shooting has actually run a little cold. He's 29th of 528 skaters in our wins added, thanks to goals that came when games were tight. NHL Edge clocks his top speed in the 99th percentile.

For context, forwards drafted around his 19th-overall slot since 2005 have scored a median 0.36 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.57. His seven goals do run ahead of his chances (5.1 expected), so expect some cooling, and SinBin.vegas is already arguing he has earned a bigger role. The last ten games say he's holding steady at about 15 minutes.
